title: "Bootstrapping Activity"
format: pdf

## The Task

A farmer has been tending to a large field of carrots and would like to evaluate their growth. The farmer has tasked you with evaluating the growth of the carrots from a random sample of their carrots!

The label on the carrots seed packet said that carrots should grow to 15cm in length. He is unsure if he is getting scammed by the Big Seed Industry and would like to get an estimate of the mean carrot length, along with a 95% plausible range. 


Suppose that seed company wasn't lying - in the entire population of carrots planted using their seeds, the average length of the carrots is 15cm. The farmer doesn't believe this, though. We need to take a sample to see if we can gain any information on the population mean using the farmer's carrots. 


## Part 1: Taking A Small Sample


The farmer has offered you a random sample of 30 carrots.

### 1.1: Population Settings

Configure the app to have the following settings:

* **Sample Size:** 20
* **Population Mean:** 15 (cm)
* **Estimator:** Mean
* **Animation Speed:** 1x

### 1.2: Take a Random Sample

**Press the Sample Carrots button**. The carrots available for you to use in your analysis will appear! Note the sample mean that outputs in the sample box.


:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 1:

* Compare the sample mean and population mean. Are they similar with this small sample size?

:::

### 1.3: Take One Bootstrap Sample

**Press the Generate 1 Bootstrap Sample button**. This will sample 30 carrots (with replacement) from your original sample. **Record the bootstrap mean here**: _______________. 


:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 2: 

* Were any carrots selected more than once? Were any carrots not selected at all? 

* What is the mean of the bootstrap sample? Is this similar or dissimilar from our original sample mean? Is this similar or dissimilar from our population mean? 
:::


### 1.4: Take Another Bootstrap Sample

**Press the Generate 1 Bootstrap Sample button** again. This will take another bootstrap sample of 30 carrots from your original sample once more. **Record the bootstrap mean here: _________**.


:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 3:
* What is the mean of this new bootstrap sample? How does it compare to the sample mean? How does it compare to the previous bootstrap mean? 

**Note: if you forgot to record your previous bootstrap mean, check the plot or click the "History" button in the Bootstrap Sample section.**
:::

### 1.5: Take Another 1000 Bootstrap Samples

**Press the Generate 1000 Bootstrap Sample button** again. This will sample 30 carrots (with replacement) from your original sample 1000 more times. Look at the plot of the bootstrap distribution. 

:::{.callout-note icon=false}

#### Peer Discussion 4:
* Where is the center of the bootstrap distribution? Is it close to the population mean, or the original sample mean? 
* Press the toggle to display the sampling distribution. How do the sampling and bootstrap distribution compare? How are they similar or different?
:::


## Part 2: Taking A Larger Sample

The farmer has graciously offered 75 new, randomly selected carrots for the analysis. 

### 2.1: Population Settings

Change the sample size to the following, leaving all other settings the same:

* **Sample Size:** 75


### 2.2: Take a Random Sample

**Press the Sample Carrots button**. The carrots available for you to use in your analysis will appear! Note the sample mean that outputs in the sample box.

:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 5: 

* Compare the sample mean and population mean. How has the relationship between the sample mean and population mean changed with the larger sample size (if at all) for this one sample?
:::


### 2.3: Take One Bootstrap Sample

**Press the Generate 1 Bootstrap Sample button**. This will sample **75** carrots (with replacement) from your original sample. **Record the bootstrap mean here**: _______________. 


:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 6: 

* How does the bootstrap mean compare to the sample mean in this larger sample size? 

:::

### 2.4: Take Another Bootstrap Sample

**Press the Generate 1 Bootstrap Sample button** again. This will take another bootstrap sample of 75 carrots from your original sample once more. **Record the bootstrap mean here: _________**.


:::{.callout-note icon=false}
#### Peer Discussion 7:
* What is the mean of this new bootstrap sample? How does it compare to the sample mean, or the first bootstrap mean? 
:::

### 2.5: Take Another 1000 Bootstrap Samples

**Press the Generate 1000 Bootstrap Sample button** again. This will sample 75 carrots (with replacement) from your original sample 1000 more times. Look at the plot of the bootstrap distribution. 

:::{.callout-note icon=false}

#### Peer Discussion 8:
* How has the relationship between the centre of the bootstrap distribution and the sampling mean changed? Are the results more or less similar with this larger sample size?

* Press the toggle to display the sampling distribution. How do the sampling and bootstrap distribution compare with this larger sample size? 
:::

### 2.6 Communicating to Farmer Clem


* Press the toggle to display the 95% Plausible Range.

:::{.callout-note icon=false}

#### Peer Discussion 9:
* Based on the sample of 75 carrots, what would you tell the farmer about the population mean of the carrot lengths? Consider the point estimate and 95% plausible range, and discuss with a peer how you would communicate this back to farmer Clem. 
:::

## Part 3: Explore the App!

Feel free to play with the settings to see how the bootstrap distribution changes. 

When interacting with the app, always:

* Decide on the settings first (maybe it would be interesting to change one at a time!)
* Press Generate Sample
* Generate bootstrap samples individually (Generate One Bootstrap Sample) or all at once (Generate 1000 Bootstrap Samples).
